katakana-chart.intro_tr: カタカナ (katakana) is one of two sound-based writing systems in Japanese and represents the exact same sounds as hiragana — the only difference between them is their field of use and shape. Katakana is primarily used for foreign-origin words (外来語[がいらいご]), foreign proper names (person/country/city names), onomatopoeia, scientific terms (plant-animal species) and words that need emphasis. It consists of a total of 46 basic characters (gojūon), by adding dakuten (゛) and handakuten (゜) to these, 25 more sounds are derived, and with small ヤユヨ, 33 compound (yōon) sounds are obtained. Additionally, special extended combinations such as ファ, ティ, ヴ have been developed to write sounds in foreign languages more accurately. This page presents all katakana characters, their derivatives and special usage rules as a single reference.

tables.caption_tr: Basic Katakana (清音[せいおん] — Gojūon Table)
footnotes_tr: シ is pronounced 'shi', チ is pronounced 'chi', ツ is pronounced 'tsu' — written in the way closest to Turkish pronunciation; these are irregular pronunciations.
フ is a sound between 'fu' and 'hu' in Turkish, produced by blowing with the lips.
ヲ is pronounced almost only as 'o' in modern Japanese and is very rarely used in practice (generally not seen in katakana texts either, hiragana を is preferred more).

tables.caption_tr: Dakuten and Handakuten Inflections (濁音[だくおん]・半濁音[はんだくおん])
footnotes_tr: ジ and ヂ are pronounced the same (ji), ズ and ヅ are pronounced the same (zu) — in modern writing, ジ and ズ are preferred almost always, ヂ/ヅ are very rare.
Dakuten (゛) is added as two short lines to the top right of the character, handakuten (゜) is added as a small circle; it can only be applied to the カ・サ・タ・ハ rows.

tables.caption_tr: Compound Sounds (拗音[ようおん] — with small ャュョ)
footnotes_tr: Small ャ/ュ/ョ is written approximately 60-70% smaller than normal-sized characters; it is aligned to the lower-middle level of the line in writing.
These sound combinations are pronounced as a single syllable, not read as two syllables (キャ = 'kya', not 'ki-ya').

tables.caption_tr: Extended Katakana — Special Combinations for Foreign Sounds
footnotes_tr: These combinations are not included in the basic 46 katakana; they were developed later solely to enable writing foreign words closer to their original pronunciation.
ヴ sound is often also pronounced/written as 'b' in speech (e.g. バイオリン is also common instead of ヴァイオリン).

tables.caption_tr: Special Marks: Long Vowel (ー) and Small ッ
rows: Uzatma işareti hiraganadaki gibi あ/い/う/え/お tekrarı değil, düz çizgidir
Sözcük sonunda ani kesilme/ünlem etkisi verir
footnotes_tr: In hiragana, the letters あ/い/う/え/お are written again for long vowels, while in katakana a straight ー line is used instead — this is an important point of difference.
The ー line is shown vertically in vertical writing (tategaki) and horizontally in horizontal writing.

dakuten-handakuten.intro_tr: Dakuten (濁点 ゛) and handakuten (半濁点 ゜) are small marks added to the upper right corner of hiragana and katakana characters and change the pronunciation of that syllable. Dakuten converts a "voiceless" (清音) sound to a "voiced" (濁音) sound: か→が, さ→ざ, た→だ, は→ば, etc. Handakuten, on the other hand, is used only in the は row and produces a "p" sound in the form は→ぱ. These marks can completely change the meaning of a word (かき "persimmon" ≠ かぎ "key"), so they must not be overlooked when reading and writing. The tables below summarize all the transformations, writing rules, and frequently confused じ/ぢ and ず/づ pairs.

tables.caption_tr: Dakuten (゛) Transformation Table — か・さ・た・は rows
rows: か[ka] き[ki] く[ku] け[ke] こ[ko]

た[ta] ち[chi] つ[tsu] て[te] と[to]

タ→ダ, チ→ヂ, ツ→ヅ, テ→デ, ト→ド

ハ→バ, ヒ→ビ, フ→ブ, ヘ→ベ, ホ→ボ
footnotes_tr: Dakuten is NOT used in the あ・な・ま・や・ら・わ rows and ん.

footnotes_tr: Handakuten (゜) is used ONLY in the は row (ha/hi/fu/he/ho); it does not appear in any other row.
In katakana, handakuten appears most frequently in words of foreign origin: パン (bread), ピアノ (piano), プール (swimming pool).

tables.caption_tr: 四[よ]つ仮名[がな] (Yotsugana) — じ/ぢ and ず/づ Confusion
rows: Varsayılan yazım; さ行 dakuten'i olarak çoğu kelimede kullanılır
Sadece: (1) aynı sesin tekrarından doğan kelimelerde (ちぢむ gibi) veya (2) 連濁[れんだく] ile ち→ぢ olduğunda

footnotes_tr: じ/ぢ and ず/づ are pronounced the same in standard Tokyo dialect; the difference is only in writing.
Modern Japanese generally prefers じ and ず; ぢ/づ are limited to exceptional cases (Monbushō 1986 rules).

small-kana-combos.title_tr: Small Kana Combinations (拗音[ようおん]) — きゃ, しゅ, ちょ...
small-kana-combos.intro_tr: In Japanese, by adding small-written や, ゆ, よ (゛や、ゅ、ょ゛) next to certain kana such as き, し, ち, に, ひ, み, り, ぎ, じ, ぢ, び, ぴ, single-syllable 'combined sounds' (拗音[ようおん] - yōon) are formed. Although these combinations are written with two kana, they are read as a single mora (sound unit); for example, きゃ is a single syllable pronounced 'kya', not two separate syllables 'ki-ya'. The small や/ゆ/よ are always written smaller than normal size in the lower right of the row; on computers, small characters (ゃゅょ) are used and must not be confused with large characters (やゆよ). The same system works in Katakana (キャ, シュ, チョ...) and additionally, extended katakana combinations (ファ, ティ, ウォ etc.) are used for writing foreign words. This topic is the natural next step for students who know Hiragana and Katakana tables, and forms the foundation of reading and writing at JLPT N5 level.

tables.caption_tr: Hiragana Small Kana Combinations — Plain (清音[せいおん])
footnotes_tr: These combinations are read as A SINGLE MORA (sound unit): きゃ = 'kya', never 'ki-ya'.
し + ゃ = しゃ 'sha' (not shi-ya), ち + ゃ = ちゃ 'cha' (not chi-ya) — in these two rows the consonant sound changes.

tables.caption_tr: Hiragana Small Kana Combinations — Voiced (濁音[だくおん]・半濁音[はんだくおん])
footnotes_tr: ぢゃ/ぢゅ/ぢょ is very rare in modern Japanese, almost never used (pronounced the same as じゃ/じゅ/じょ, appearing only in certain compound words).
じゃ and ぢゃ are pronounced the same ('ja') but have different spellings — the rule distinguishing this difference is related to the 連濁[れんだく] rule in the Dakuten/Handakuten topic.

tables.caption_tr: Katakana Small Kana Combinations (Exactly the Same Logic as Hiragana)
footnotes_tr: Katakana is normally used for foreign words, country/city names, and onomatopoeia.
Example words: キャベツ (cabbage), シャワー (shower), チョコレート (chocolate), ジュース (juice).

tables.caption_tr: Extended Katakana Combinations (For Foreign Sounds — Not in the Standard Hiragana Table)
footnotes_tr: These combinations are NOT in the standard 拗音[ようおん] list; they were developed specifically for katakana only to write foreign words more accurately.
Some authors/publishers may prefer to write with the nearest standard katakana instead of using these extended combinations (e.g., in older texts ハン might appear instead of ファン).

tables.caption_tr: Spelling Rules and Common Mistakes
rows: Büyük や yazılırsa 'ki-ya' (iki hece) olarak okunur, birleşim bozulur.
El yazısında küçük kana belirgin şekilde daha küçük ve satırın alt-sağına yakın yazılmalı.
し + ゃ birleşiminde temel ünsüz korunur ama 'i' sesi düşer, 'sh' + 'a' = 'sha' olur.
Günlük kelimelerin neredeyse tamamında じゃ/じゅ/じょ kullanılır; ぢゃ sadece birkaç özel durumda (連濁[れんだく]) görülür.
っ ile ゃゅょ karıştırma
Küçük っ (sokuon, çift ünsüz) tamamen farklı bir işleve sahiptir — bu konu ayrı olarak 'Uzun Ünlüler ve Küçük っ' başlığında işlenir.
Bilgisayar/telefon klavyesinde birleşimler doğrudan 'kya', 'sha', 'cho' gibi yazılarak otomatik üretilir.

wa-topic-particle.intro_tr: は (written as 'ha', read as わ when used as a particle) is one of the most fundamental particles in Japanese and marks the TOPIC (topic) of the sentence — that is, it adds the meaning of 'I'm talking about...'. は should not be confused with the grammatical subject (subject) in English; the particle that marks the actual subject is が, and は instead establishes the frame of 'what I'm going to say about this topic'. は also establishes contrast/comparison, makes known/given information a topic again, and is also used to emphasize a certain element in negative sentences. It can replace particles like を and が, and is attached on top of particles like に/で/と/から/まで. The most frequently encountered pattern at N5 level is the structure X は Y です (X is Y).

tables.caption_tr: Basic Functions of the は Particle
rows: 私[わたし]は田中[たなか]です。
X は A, Y は B
犬[いぬ]は好[す]きですが、猫[ねこ]は好[す]きではありません。
"Köpekleri severim ama kedileri sevmem." İki は birbirine zıt bilgi verir.
(を/が düşer) X は …ません
肉[にく]は食[た]べません。
"Eti yemiyorum (ama başka şey yiyebilirim)" — を yerine は gelerek belirli bir şey vurgulanır.
その本[ほん]は面白[おもしろ]いです。
Konuşmada daha önce geçmiş veya bağlamdan bilinen bir şey tekrar konu edilir.
Çift konu yapısı (X は Y が …)
象[ぞう]は鼻[はな]が長[なが]い。
"Fillerin hortumu uzundur." は geniş konuyu, が alt-özneyi belirtir.
X は Y だ/です
日本[にほん]は島国[しまぐに]です。
"Japonya bir ada ülkesidir." Genel bilgi/gerçek ifadesi.

tables.caption_tr: Basic Differences Between は and が
rows: Cümlenin geri kalanı (yüklem) hakkında bilgi verir
Bilinen, verilmiş, konuşmada zaten geçen bilgi
Yeni bilgi, ilk kez tanıtılan bilgi
だれは, なには gibi kullanılmaz ✗
だれが、なにが — soru kelimesi genelde が alır ✓
Yan (bağımlı) cümlelerde özne çoğunlukla が alır
私[わたし]は学生[がくせい]です。(Genel tanıtım)
私[わたし]が学生[がくせい]です。("Öğrenci olan BENİM" — vurgulu, seçici)
footnotes_tr: Briefly: は = 'I'm talking about this', and が = 'this exactly (not something else)'

tables.caption_tr: Combining は with Other Particles
rows: を düşer, sadece は kalır
パンを食[た]べる → パンは食[た]べない。
を + は birlikte kullanılmaz, を tamamen kaybolur.
が düşer, sadece は kalır
猫[ねこ]がいる → 猫[ねこ]はいる。
東京[とうきょう]に行[い]く → 東京[とうきょう]には行[い]かない。
に korunur, üzerine は eklenir.
図書館[としょかん]で勉強[べんきょう]する → 図書館[としょかん]では勉強[べんきょう]しない。
で korunur, üzerine は eklenir.
彼[かれ]と話[はな]す → 彼[かれ]とは話[はな]さない。
9時[くじ]から始[はじ]まる → 9時[くじ]からは始[はじ]まらない。
駅[えき]まで歩[ある]く → 駅[えき]までは歩[ある]かない。
も zaten kendi başına 'de/da/aynı zamanda' işlevini üstlenir, は ile yan yana gelmez.

tables.caption_tr: Basic は Patterns with the です Copula
rows: X は Y です (olumlu, şimdiki/geniş)
これは辞書[じしょ]です。
X は Y ではありません (olumsuz)
これは辞書[じしょ]ではありません。
X は Y でした (geçmiş olumlu)
昨日[きのう]は雨[あめ]でした。
X は Y ではありませんでした (geçmiş olumsuz)
テストは簡単[かんたん]ではありませんでした。
X は Y ですか (soru)
これは山田[やまだ]さんのペンですか。
X は Y が好[す]きです (tercih)
私[わたし]は寿司[すし]が好[す]きです。
X は Y があります/います (sahiplik/varlık)
私[わたし]は兄[あに]がいます。

tables.caption_tr: Common Mistakes and Correct Usage
rows: Soru kelimeleri (だれ, 何[なに], どこ vb.) genellikle が alır, は almaz.
は her zaman özne demektir sanmak ✗
は konu, が genellikle gramatik özne bildirir
は+が bir arada kullanılabilir: 私[わたし]は音楽[おんがく]が好[す]きです (konu: ben, özne: müzik).
を ile は yan yana gelmez, を tamamen düşer.
猫[ねこ]がは可愛[かわい]い ✗
猫[ねこ]は可愛[かわい]い ✓

examples.target: 私[わたし]は学生[がくせい]です。
examples.reading: わたしはがくせいです。
examples.translation_tr: I am a student.

examples.target: これは本[ほん]です。
examples.reading: これはほんです。
examples.translation_tr: This is a book.

examples.target: 今日[きょう]は暑[あつ]いです。
examples.reading: きょうはあついです。
examples.translation_tr: Today is hot (we are talking about today as the topic).

examples.target: 象[ぞう]は鼻[はな]が長[なが]い。
examples.reading: ぞうははながながい。
examples.translation_tr: As for elephants, their trunks are long. — Example of the paired は/が structure.
examples.note_tr: は marks the general topic of the sentence (象/elephant), while が marks the sub-subject (鼻/trunk) within that topic.

examples.target: これは好[す]きではありません。
examples.reading: これはすきではありません。
examples.translation_tr: I don't like this (but I might like something else — emphasis on contrast/opposition).
examples.note_tr: The object これ doesn't normally take を, but は makes it an emphasized topic.

examples.target: 東京[とうきょう]には行[い]きません。
examples.reading: とうきょうにはいきません。
examples.translation_tr: I'm not going to Tokyo (but I might go somewhere else).
examples.note_tr: に + は combines to form には; に doesn't disappear, は is attached on top of it.

examples.target: 田中[たなか]さんは先生[せんせい]ではありません。
examples.reading: たなかさんはせんせいではありません。
examples.translation_tr: Tanaka is not a teacher.

examples.target: 私[わたし]は日本語[にほんご]を勉強[べんきょう]していますが、彼[かれ]は英語[えいご]を勉強[べんきょう]しています。
examples.reading: わたしはにほんごをべんきょうしていますが、かれはえいごをべんきょうしています。
examples.translation_tr: I am studying Japanese, and he is studying English.
examples.note_tr: Using two は side by side compares two different topics (contrast function).

ga-subject-particle.title_tr: が Subject Particle (Difference with は)
ga-subject-particle.intro_tr: が and は are the two particles most commonly confused in Japanese; although both may sometimes appear as "subject," they actually perform different functions: は indicates the TOPIC of the sentence (what is being talked about), while が marks the grammatical SUBJECT, especially NEW information that the listener does not yet know. While は operates on the logic of "known/old information + broad topic," が emphasizes with the nuance "this is it, exactly this," highlighting a specific element. Question words (誰[だれ], 何[なに], どこ) always use が when they are the subject; in expressions of feeling/ability like 好[す]き, 欲[ほ]しい, わかる, the true "object" is marked with が. Subjects within subordinate clauses (relative clauses, causal clauses) also almost always take が, not は. This page summarizes all the basic rules, mandatory usage areas, and common mistakes of the two particles in table form.

tables.caption_tr: Basic Usage Areas of が
rows: Konuşmada ilk kez geçen, dinleyicinin bilmediği özneyi belirtir

誰[だれ], 何[なに], どこ, いつ gibi soru kelimeleri özne olduğunda daima が kullanılır; だれは yanlıştır
誰[だれ]が来[き]ましたか。(Kim geldi?)
好[す]き, 嫌[きら]い, 欲[ほ]しい, わかる, できる gibi kalıplarda asıl nesne が ile işaretlenir
私[わたし]は日本語[にほんご]がわかります。(Ben Japonca anlarım.)
見[み]える, 聞[き]こえる gibi kendiliğinden gerçekleşen algı fiillerinde özne が alır
富士山[ふじさん]が見[み]えます。(Fuji Dağı görünüyor.)
O anda gözlemlenen, önceden bahsedilmemiş bir durumu bildirirken
あ、雨[あめ]が降[ふ]っています。(Ah, yağmur yağıyor!)
Bir isme bağlı yan cümlecik içindeki özne が ile işaretlenir, は kullanılmaz
これは私[わたし]が作[つく]ったケーキです。(Bu benim yaptığım pasta.)

rows: 誰[だれ]は好[す]きですか。
誰[だれ]が好[す]きですか。
Soru kelimesi özne olduğunda が zorunludur
(Kapıyı çalan biri varken) あ、人[ひと]は来[き]ました。
あ、人[ひと]が来[き]ました。
Anlık, yeni bir gözlem olduğu için が kullanılır
これは私[わたし]は作[つく]ったケーキです。
これは私[わたし]が作[つく]ったケーキです。
İsmi niteleyen alt cümlecik içindeki özne は değil が alır
象[ぞう]が鼻[はな]は長[なが]い。 (genel bilgi bağlamında)
象[ぞう]は鼻[はな]が長[なが]い。
Büyük konu は, o konuya ait ayrıntı ise が ile verilir

o-object-particle.intro_tr: The を particle is a basic object particle used in Japanese to mark the direct object of a verb (that is, the thing directly affected by an action) and is only used with transitive (他動詞[たどうし]) verbs. Within a sentence, it always comes immediately after the object and immediately before the verb: [Object] + を + [Verb]. The を particle is also used in the meanings of 'a place/path passed through' (with motion verbs like 歩く, 渡る, 飛ぶ) and 'a point departed from/left' (with verbs like 出る, 降りる, 卒業する) — in these cases it is translated not as '-i/-ı' but as '-den/-dan', or as prepositions such as 'inside' or 'on'. In writing, を is always written in hiragana; in katakana texts it can also be written as ヲ, but its pronunciation is always 'o' (not 'wo'). In everyday speech, especially with objects that are well-known/easily guessed, を is sometimes completely dropped.

tables.caption_tr: 1. Basic Usage: を + Transitive Verb (Direct Object)
rows: 日本語[にほんご]を勉強する
にほんごをべんきょうする
footnotes_tr: Sentence order is always: [Object] + を + [Verb]. The noun before を is the thing that directly receives/is affected by the action.

tables.caption_tr: 2. Special Uses of を: With Motion Verbs (Path/Passage, Point of Departure)
rows: 歩[ある]く, 渡[わた]る, 通[とお]る, 飛[と]ぶ, 走[はし]る
出[で]る, 降[お]りる, 卒業[そつぎょう]する
電車[でんしゃ]を降りる
大学[だいがく]を卒業する
だいがくをそつぎょうする
footnotes_tr: In these uses, を translates to Turkish as '-de/-da' (passage) or '-den/-dan' (departure), not as '-i/-ı'.
These verbs are generally considered intransitive (自動詞[じどうし]) but they take を; this is an exceptional structure and must be memorized.

tables.caption_tr: 3. Comparison with Confusing Particles: を / が / に / で
rows: Özne, ya da beğenme/isteme fiillerinde nesne (好き, 欲しい, わかる)
が duygu/algı/yeterlilik fiilleriyle kullanılır, を değil
Hedef, yön, varış noktası, zaman noktası
に hareketin yöneldiği/ulaştığı noktayı gösterir, を geçilen yolu gösterir
公園[こうえん]で遊[あそ]ぶ (parkta oynamak)
で eylemin yapıldığı sabit yeri, を bazı hareket fiilleriyle geçilen yolu gösterir
footnotes_tr: Common mistake: 公園を散歩[さんぽ]する (walking around inside the park) and 公園で遊ぶ (playing in the park) are different — one is passage/strolling, the other is an action in a fixed place.

tables.caption_tr: 4. Omission of を in Everyday Spoken Language
rows: Rahat/samimi konuşmada, özellikle nesne cümle başındaysa を sıkça düşürülür
Soru cümlelerinde de düşürülebilir, tonlama nesneyi belirginleştirir
footnotes_tr: In formal writing or N5 exam questions, を should never be omitted; this only occurs in spoken/casual recordings.

ni-particle.intro_tr: The に particle is one of the most frequently used particles with the most functions at N5 level; therefore, it can be thought of as "a versatile multi-purpose particle that works for everything." Fundamentally, it is used to indicate a point in time (hour, day, date), the destination of movement (with 行く/来る/帰る), the location where something is (with ある/いる), the target/indirect object of an action (giving something to someone, saying, teaching), and the result of a change. The confusion of に with other particles such as へ, で, を is a very common mistake among Turkish learners; therefore, these particles are compared with each other in the tables below. The logic behind the rule is as follows: に generally indicates "a fixed point" (a moment in time, a destination/location in space), while で generally indicates "the area where the action takes place." Instead of memorizing the tables on this page, first look at which verb it is used with and try to identify its function.
